 This new, interactive experience in the heart of downtown brings thousands of years of Chattanooga and Hamilton County history to life—from our region’s earliest inhabitants to the people, places, and events that shaped the community we know today.
 Even better, local high school and college students helped build it, gaining real-world experience while helping tell the story of their own community.
 Thank you to Linda Moss Mines, Tom Griscom, John Edwards, Emily Mack, Zach Wamp, Isaiah Smallman, the Dynamo students, and everyone who helped bring this vision to life.
 Now it’s your turn to experience our history!

 Through matching 1:1 reimbursable grants, Scenic Storefronts helps local businesses invest in the spaces they need to open, grow, and thrive downtown. And the impact extends beyond each individual storefront: these investments contribute to a more vibrant, welcoming downtown for everyone. 
 Thank you to the City of Chattanooga for continuing to support this program. Learn more about Scenic Storefronts and apply at www.rivercitycompany.com/scenic-storefronts

items.content_text:
Among G7 economies, real household income per capita increased by 0.2% in Q1 2026, reflecting varied outcomes across countries. 
 Real GDP per capita in the United Kingdom increased by 0.6% after two quarters with no growth. 
 Among other #OECD countries, the largest increases in real household income per capita were recorded in Hungary and Chile. 
 GDP growth focuses on the change in aggregate economic activity, while household income growth reflects the change in income earned by households such as the income available for spending or saving. 
 Learn more: https://brnw.ch/21x576e
 #OECDstats

items.content_text: A hazardous substance found inside a Hixson home will be removed by authorities. Chattanooga Police and Fire responded to the 400 block of Northmont Road Friday (8/21/26) morning at 11:24 AM after a homeowner discovered an old bottle in their garage containing a hazardous substance- Diethyl Ether Anhydrous. A small evacuation of four homes was initiated as a safety measure, including the home involved. Other neighbors have been asked to shelter in place. Chattanooga Police Department EOD will be assisting CFD Special Operations in the removal of the substance. Part of Northmont Road is closed to traffic for the time being. No airborne hazards or other safety threats are involved in this incident.

The Urban League of Greater Chattanooga hosted its 11th annual Entrepreneur Power Luncheon this week.
 We were honored to have Chef Jason Gardner as our keynote speaker. Jason Darnell Gardner, known as Chef JGardner, is a Memphis native and founder of TrapFusion901, a restaurant celebrated for its creative and healthy soul food. His culinary journey began at age seven with his grandmother’s influence, leading to the opening of Trap Fusion in Whitehaven in 2019. After studying Biology at The University of Tennessee at Chattanooga, he explored various entrepreneurial ventures, including event planning and the launch of BeLeaf Cigars. In 2018, he returned to cooking with a food truck, quickly gaining a loyal following. Today, Chef JGardner caters to celebrities and remains dedicated to investing in his community.
 We also honored two local entrepreneurs!
 ULGC’s New Business of the Year: Darryl Eubanks II, the founder and owner of Still Life Athletics 
 ULGC’s Business of the Year: Cheryl Key, John P. Franklin Funeral Home 
 We would also like to thank our presenting sponsor, EPB; Capital Access Sponsors, Pinnacle Financial Partners, Tennessee Valley Federal Credit Union, and Hamilton County Mayor’s Office!
 Images:  Final Flash Productions

 You may also know her as “Wanda the Program Lady” at Chattanooga Lookouts games, where she has been a familiar face since 1990.
 This week, Wanda was inducted into the Bessie Smith Cultural Center Hall of Fame in recognition of her contributions to the Chattanooga community.
 Her secret to staying positive? “I don’t meet no strangers. I just enjoy people.”
 We’re proud to call Ms. Wanda a Moc and grateful for all the ways she has helped make UTC and Chattanooga feel like home. 💙💛

items.title: Congratulations to Herbert “Book” McCray for being featured in Celebrate Chattanooga African Americans Spotlight!  Celeb...
items.content_text:
Congratulations to Herbert “Book” McCray for being featured in Celebrate Chattanooga African Americans Spotlight! 
 Celebrate Chattanooga proudly recognizes Mr, McCray, whose remarkable journey from championship basketball player to educator, administrator and longtime mentor demonstrates the power of turning personal achievement into service to others.
 Read the full story: https://www.celebratechattanooga.com/.../herbert-%22book...
**CELEBRATE CHATTANOOGA AFRICAN AMERICANS SPOTLIGHT**
 Herbert “Book” McCray
 **Educator • National Champion • Mentor • Community Leader**
 Celebrate Chattanooga proudly recognizes **Herbert “Book” McCray**, whose remarkable journey from championship basketball player to educator, administrator and longtime mentor demonstrates the power of turning personal achievement into service to others.
 A native of Louisville, Kentucky, McCray came to Chattanooga as a student-athlete at the University of Tennessee at Chattanooga. He became part of an important era in UTC basketball history and was a key senior leader on the **1977 NCAA Division II National Championship team**.
 But the championship was only one chapter of his Chattanooga story.
 McCray earned bachelor's and master's degrees in education from UTC and an Education Specialist degree in Educational Leadership from Tennessee Technological University. During a 26-year career in Hamilton County schools, he served children and families as a classroom teacher, coach and school administrator.
 In 1992, he founded what began as the **Chattanooga Basketball Foundation**. Through leagues, camps, tournaments and other activities, the organization reached thousands of children and families. Over time, the mission grew beyond basketball into **Boys To Men: A Male Mentoring Model**, now an outreach of the Bethlehem Center.
 Boys To Men focuses on the personal, social and spiritual development of young men, building relationships and helping prepare them for high school graduation and successful postsecondary futures. The program's roots now extend more than three decades.
 McCray's commitment to education also includes credentialing as a Dropout Prevention Specialist and sharing his work with other educators and professionals.
 His lifetime of service continues to be recognized. In 2026, McCray received the **Walt Lauter Male Lifetime Achievement Award from the Greater Chattanooga Sports Hall of Fame**.
 **A Personal Note from Celebrate Chattanooga**
 This spotlight is also personal.
 When my husband, children, and I returned home to Chattanooga from Memphis, Mr. McCray was one of the first education administrators we encountered as we entered the Chattanooga-Hamilton County school system. Our arrival came after the regular school registration period, and he graciously welcomed us and helped my children find an educational home at Chattanooga's 21st Century school.
 Years later, I recognize that encounter as something much larger than one family's school-registration experience.
 It was a glimpse of the same quality that has characterized Herbert “Book” McCray's life's work: **seeing young people, helping families and opening doors.**
 From helping make history on a championship basketball court, to educating children in Chattanooga's schools, to mentoring generations of young men, his story reminds us that a person's greatest victories are not necessarily the ones recorded on a scoreboard.
 Sometimes, they are recorded in the lives of the people who were helped along the way.
 **Celebrate Chattanooga African Americans salutes Herbert “Book” McCray — educator, champion, mentor and community servant — for a legacy that continues to help move Chattanooga forward.**
 Learn more at https://www.celebratechattanooga.com/…/herbert-%22book%22-m…

Now Accepting Proposals in #EastRidgeTN! 💻
 Website Design, Content Management System & Hosting Services
 The City of East Ridge is now accepting proposals from qualified firms for the redesign of the City’s public-facing website, www.EastRidgeTN.gov, along with Content Management System (CMS), hosting, and ongoing support services.
 Through this project, the City is seeking a modern, accessible, secure, and user-friendly website that improves how residents, businesses, visitors, and community partners access information, connect with City services, and stay informed about what’s happening throughout East Ridge.
 Project Scope Includes:
 ✔️ Website redesign and development
 ✔️ Content Management System (CMS)
 ✔️ Content migration and organization
 ✔️ Mobile-responsive and user-friendly design
 ✔️ ADA accessibility and compliance
 ✔️ Website hosting, security, and ongoing support
 ✔️ Improved access to City information and online services
 🗓️ Proposal Deadline:
 Monday, September 14, 2026 at 3:00pm EST 
 📍 Proposal Submission:
 Proposals must be submitted in accordance with the requirements outlined in the RFP to:
 City of East Ridge
 ATTN: City Clerk’s Office
 1517 Tombras Avenue
 East Ridge, TN 37412
 Proposals must be received no later than 3:00pm EST on Monday, September 14, 2026.
 📄 Request for Proposals & Submission Requirements: 
 Interested firms can review the complete Request for Proposals, including the project scope, requirements, evaluation criteria, and submission instructions, here:
 https://www.eastridgetn.gov/…/business_economic_dev_31_1708…
 ❓ Questions: 
 Questions regarding the RFP and proposal requirements should be submitted in accordance with the instructions provided in the RFP.
 For additional information, contact CMcAllister@EastRidgeTN.gov.
 We look forward to receiving your proposal and taking the next step toward a new and improved EastRidgeTN.gov! 💻

HCSO Arrests Man for Violating School Zone Speed Limit, DUI
 Hamilton County, TN – On the morning of August 19, 2026, HCSO Traffic Investigators conducting school-zone traffic enforcement initiated a traffic stop after observing a vehicle traveling at 37 MPH in a 20 MPH school zone on Hunter Road.
 The driver, Glenn Herrera-Morales, appeared to be under the influence of alcohol, and multiple alcoholic beverage containers were found in his vehicle.
 Herrera-Morales was taken into custody and charged with the following:
 • Speeding in a School Zone
 • Driving Under the Influence
 • Open Container Law
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Brush Collection Day is coming up for some! See below for more information.
Wednesday, August 26 is Brush Collection Day for some residents of Collegedale. 
 Helpful Reminders: 😀😀😀
 *Brush collection should not exceed a standard load (5x8).
 *Please organize/stack/bag the brush items.
 *Brush collection services are for tree trimming, not tree cutting or removal. Private arrangements must be made for disposal of major tree cutting and lot clearing.
 *No stumps or roots mixed with dirt.
 *Please make sure to use biodegradable bags for leaves, yard clippings or small bushes.
 *Please have brush out by 7 am on your collection day. Brush shall not be placed by the curb prior to the weekend before date of service.
 *Brush collection days are either every second or fourth Wednesday of each month. Please check our website www.collegedaletn.gov for your scheduled and our holiday schedule. 
 *Any storm damage should be reported 2 days of said storm.
 *Maximum 8 feet in length and nothing larger than 9 inches in diameter. 
 *No construction material or remodeling materials, such as decking, fencing, wooden pallets, boards, etc. See less See less See less See less See less

🏡 How well do you know Fort Wood?
 One of Chattanooga’s most architecturally distinctive historic neighborhoods is getting some well-deserved attention in The Pulse.
 This neighborhood spotlight explores Fort Wood’s evolution from a Civil War-era fortification to one of Chattanooga’s most fashionable residential neighborhoods, with homes representing Queen Anne, Tudor Revival, Romanesque Revival, Spanish Colonial Revival, and other architectural styles. The district was listed in the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.
 Fort Wood is a great reminder that Chattanooga’s historic neighborhoods aren’t simply collections of beautiful buildings—they tell the story of how our city grew and changed over generations.
 We’re always glad to see Chattanooga’s architectural history in the spotlight. Take a few minutes to read the article and learn a little more about this remarkable neighborhood.
 👉 Read “Neighborhood Spotlight: Learning A Little History About The Fort Wood District” in The Pulse: https://www.chattanoogapulse.com/…/neighborhood-spotlight-…/
 #PreserveChattanooga #FortWood #ChattanoogaHistory #HistoricPreservation #Chattanooga #thisishistoric

🏘️ Red Bank Neighborhood Associations — We Want to Connect With You!
 Does your Red Bank neighborhood have a neighborhood association, homeowners group, or organized community group? The City of Red Bank’s Community Development Department wants to hear from you!
 We are building a stronger, more direct connection with neighborhoods across our community so residents can stay informed and have opportunities to be involved in the issues and initiatives that affect where they live.
 Why does this matter?
 Community engagement works best when communication goes both ways. Neighborhood associations can help us:
 • 📣 Share information about upcoming public engagement opportunities, workshops, and community meetings
 • 🏘️ Better understand neighborhood priorities, concerns, and ideas
 • 🌱 Connect residents with planning, development, parks, stormwater, transportation, and other community initiatives
 • 💬 Create meaningful opportunities for residents to provide input before decisions are made
 • 🤝 Build stronger partnerships between neighborhoods, residents, and the City 
 Whether your association is large or small, formally organized or simply a group of neighbors working together, we want to connect with you.
 👉 If your neighborhood has an association or organized community group, please reach out to the Community Development Department at bpowell@redbanktn.gov and let us know where you are, who you are and how we can directly communicate.
 Together, we can make sure Red Bank’s neighborhoods are not just informed about their community’s future — they are part of shaping it.
 Your neighborhood. Your voice. Your Red Bank.
 #RedBankTN #CommunityDevelopment #NeighborhoodEngagement #CommunityMatters #YourVoiceYourRedBank

items.content_text:
The Chattanooga Preservation Plan will help guide how preservation can be used as a tool to support Chattanooga and Hamilton County’s growth while protecting and enhancing the places that make our communities special. Most importantly, the plan will be shaped by the community itself  through a process guided by preservation professionals.
 A public workshop and concepts testing session will take place on Monday, August 24, from 4:30–6:00 p.m. in the First Floor Auditorium of the Downtown Chattanooga Public Library. This session marks Phase 3 of the five-phase planning process and is an important opportunity to help shape the recommendations that will ultimately be included in the final plan.
 During the workshop, our consultant team will share findings from the community survey and lead discussions around preservation issues, priorities, and potential strategies. Your perspective would be particularly valuable as we begin moving from community input toward specific recommendations.
 A new preservation plan for Chattanooga is made possible through generous support from the Lyndhurst Foundation and the Tennessee Historical Commission. The process is being led by the Walker Collaborative in partnership with Thomason and Associates and Common Ground.
 Please let us know if you plan to attend. Feel free to drop in as your schedule allows. Quick RSVP: https://forms.gle/MBrow2LV24QUvExP8

🚨🚨PROMOTED: LIEUTENANT JOSH BOOTH🚨🚨
 Please join us in congratulating Josh Booth on his promotion to Lieutenant!
 Lt. Booth has served Collegedale for more than 12 years, beginning his law enforcement career as a volunteer Reserve Officer and steadily advancing through the ranks through service, leadership, and continued professional growth.
 Along the way, he has served as a patrol officer, shift supervisor, and in command-level leadership. He has also taken on numerous responsibilities critical to our department, overseeing all agency training programs and instructors, as well as the trainers and probationary officers in our Field Training Program. He also manages property, evidence, equipment, and other essential resources that equip our officers to better serve the Collegedale community.
 Lt. Booth also completed the distinguished FBI-LEEDA Trilogy leadership series last year and is currently pursuing a master’s degree in public safety.
 As our Operations Division Commander, Lt. Booth leads one of the most important areas of our department and continues to help shape our officers, their training, and all operations and logistics that support our mission every day.
 From volunteer Reserve Officer to Lieutenant, his career path continues to provide a strong example of what our motto #ServiceBeforeSelf means.
 Congratulations, Lieutenant Booth, on a well-earned promotion! If you see him around Collegedale, be sure to congratulate him!

A public workshop and concepts testing session will take place on Monday, August 24, from 4:30–6:00 p.m. in the First Floor Auditorium of the Downtown Chattanooga Public Library. This session marks Phase 3 of the five-phase planning process and is an important opportunity to help shape the recommendations that will ultimately be included in the final plan.
During the workshop, our consultant team will share findings from the community survey and lead discussions around preservation issues, priorities, and potential strategies. Your perspective would be particularly valuable as we begin moving from community input toward specific recommendations.
A new preservation plan for Chattanooga is made possible through generous support from the Lyndhurst Foundation and the Tennessee Historical Commission. The process is being led by the Walker Collaborative in partnership with Thomason and Associates and Common Ground.

Congratulations to Lieutenant Allen Green on receiving the prestigious 2026 Company Officer of the Year award through the International Association of Fire Chiefs!
 Lt. Green was recognized at the International Association of Fire Chiefs conference in Kansas City and again tonight by the Chattanooga City Council. He is redefining fire service leadership. Beyond his work as a fire inspector, he is a dedicated educator and mentor who consistently works to create lasting change in our community. From founding the nonprofit PPCH, Inc. (Pain, Perseverance, Character, Hope) to mentoring at-risk youth and launching literacy initiatives like "Read to Succeed," his commitment to serving others is inspiring. He even wrote a children’s book to teach kids about fire safety. 
 Thank you, Lt. Green, for demonstrating that true leadership means helping others rise!
